# Emissions Clock

> A live, browser-based clock estimating carbon dioxide (CO₂) and methane emissions so far this year for the world and major emitting countries. URL: https://ramialbatal.github.io/emissions-clock/

## What it shows
- World and per-country emissions emitted so far in the current year, ticking every second.
- Countries: China, United States, India, European Union, Russia, Japan, Iran, Indonesia, Saudi Arabia, South Korea, Germany, Canada, Mexico, Brazil, Türkiye, South Africa, Australia, United Kingdom, plus rest of world.
- For each: share of world total, tonnes per second, latest official annual figure, projected figure for the current year, emissions per person, year-on-year trend, and history since 2015.
- A switch between CO₂ and methane, and a plain-language explanation of how each gas causes warming.

## Data sources (fetched live from Our World in Data)
- CO₂: Global Carbon Project, Global Carbon Budget — fossil fuels and cement, territorial, excluding land-use change. https://ourworldindata.org/co2-emissions
- Methane: Jones et al., National contributions to climate change — all human sources, in CO₂-equivalents (100-year GWP). https://ourworldindata.org/methane-emissions

## Method
The latest official annual value is projected to the current year using the latest year-on-year change, then spread evenly across the year: emitted so far = projected annual total × fraction of the year elapsed (UTC). The live counters are a model, not a real-time measurement.

## Source code
